title: Christ Is Born, Go Forth to Meet Him
description: Christ Is Born, Go Forth to Meet Him in Tonic Solfa to KALMAR, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns of the Greek Church (Edinburgh and London, 1900), where he gives them as “By St. Cosmas, 760 A.D”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in 8.7.8.7.7.7, and this page sets them to KALMAR; any other 8.7.8.7.7.7 tune fits them as well.
underlay: Christ is born, go forth to meet Him, Christ by all the heaven a-dored; Sing-ing songs of wel-come, greet Him, For the earth re-ceives her Lord. All ye na-tions shout and sing; For He comes, your glo-rious King.

lines: Christ is born, go forth to meet Him,
Christ by all the heaven adored;
Singing songs of welcome, greet Him,
For the earth receives her Lord.
All ye nations shout and sing;
For He comes, your glorious King.
Once His heavenly image bearing,
Man has sunk to depths of sin;
Now defiled, debased, despairing,
Clad in rags and foul within;
But our God, who beauty gave,
Lifts the soul He comes to save.
From the height of heaven beholding,
Pity filled the heart of grace,
And our Lord, His love unfolding,
Made the earth His dwelling-place;
And a virgin mother gave
God Incarnate, man to save.
Wisdom, Might, and Word Eternal,
Glory of the Father, Thou!
Hid from man and powers supernal,
Lo, He wears our nature now!
To the Lord your worship bring,
Praise Him, your victorious King.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Greek Church (1900)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Greek Church; set to KALMAR by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
